'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Jihadist insurgency in Niger]]
**Five people are killed and 19 more injured during an [[ambush]] by gunmen at a convoy in the [[Tillabéri Region]], [[Niger]]. Two attackers are killed in the ensuing [[shootout]]. [https://www.voanews.com/amp/killed-in-suspected-jihadi-attack-in-niger-/7182446.html (VOA)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[2023 Hollywood labor disputes]]
**[[2023 SAG-AFTRA strike]]
***[[Universal Pictures|Universal]] announces that the upcoming [[Red carpet fashion|red carpet]] [[premiere]] for the ''[[Oppenheimer (film)|Oppenheimer]]'' film has been cancelled amidst the [[SAG-AFTRA]] strikes. The film is still expected to be screened. [https://www.screendaily.com/news/universal-cancels-oppenheimer-new-york-red-carpet-as-actors-strike-kicks-off/5184062.article (''Screen International'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Foxconn]], a tech giant headquartered in Taiwan, announces that it has made a deal with [[Karnataka]], a state in [[India]], to buy 300 acres of land for a new [[iPhone]] factory. [https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/technology/legal-hurdles-cleared-foxconn-to-get-300-acre-plot-near-bengaluru-airport-for-iphone-facility-soon/articleshow/101762429.cms (''Economic Times'')]

'''International relations''' 
*[[Nagorno-Karabakh conflict]]
**[[Armenia–Azerbaijan border crisis (2021–present)|Armenia–Azerbaijan border crisis]]
***[[Azerbaijan]]'s [[State Border Service of Azerbaijan|State Border Service]] reopens the [[Lachin corridor]] to allow the [[International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement|Red Cross]] to conduct [[medical evacuation]]s from [[Nagorno-Karabakh]] to [[Armenia]] amid protests over the corridor's closure on July 11 and humanitarian concerns. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20230714-red-cross-restarts-karabakh-evacuations-after-protests-over-blockade (AFP via France 24)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Gilgo Beach serial killings]]
**A suspect in the [[Long Island]] [[serial murder]]s is arrested in [[Massapequa Park, New York|Massapequa Park]], [[New York (state)|New York]], [[United States]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/crime/gilgo-beach-serial-killer-arrested-long-island-b2375376.html (''The Independent'')]
*[[Protests against Quran desecration in Sweden]]
**[[Swedish Police Authority|Police]] authorize a protest involving the [[Desecration|burning]] of the [[Bible]] and the [[Torah]] outside the [[List of diplomatic missions of Israel|Israeli embassy]] in [[Stockholm]] following a series of [[Criticism of Islam|anti-Islam]] demonstrations involving [[Quran desecration]] across [[Sweden|the country]]. [[Israel]]i officials have urged the [[Swedish government]] to prevent the act. [https://apnews.com/article/sweden-burning-quran-bible-torah-59c286340400b685d112d506f942b79d (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2023 Cambodian general election]]
**Two members of the [[Opposition (politics)|opposition]] [[Candlelight Party]] are arrested for allegedly encouraging voters to [[Spoilt vote|spoil ballots]] ahead of the election. [https://guardian.ng/news/world/cambodia-arrests-two-opposition-members-over-ballot-protest/ (AFP via ''The Guardian'')]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Japanese space program]]
**An [[Epsilon (rocket)#Epsilon S|Epsilon S]] [[solid-propellant rocket]] upper stage, an upgraded version of [[JAXA]]'s [[Epsilon (rocket)|Epsilon]] launch vehicle, explodes about a minute after [[Rocket engine#Ignition|ignition]] during a test in [[Akita Prefecture]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/japan-rocket-test-fail-epsilon-jaxa-space-3628686 (AFP via CNA)]
*The [[ISRO|Indian Space Research Organization]] launches [[Chandrayaan-3]] on a mission to the [[Moon]]. The mission will deploy the [[Vikram (spacecraft)|Vikram lander]] and [[Pragyan (rover)|Pragyan rover]] to study the Moon's surface for two weeks. The mission is similar to the failed [[Chandrayaan-2]] mission, which crashed shortly before landing in 2019. [https://www.space.com/india-launches-chandrayaan-3-moon-landing-mission (Space.com)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2023 Pacific Four Series]]
**In [[women's rugby union]], [[New Zealand women's national rugby union team|New Zealand]] win their second consecutive [[Pacific Four Series]] title after defeating the [[United States women's national rugby union team|United States]] 39–17 at [[TD Place Stadium]] in [[Ottawa]], [[Ontario]], [[Canada]]. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/rugby-union/66209800 (BBC Sport)]
